text: Skill Center（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：在设置页集中管理 DSH 技能。它扫描 DSH 全局及项目技能目录，并通过设置面板和主机 API 查看技能详情、开关技能、创建技能、从链接安装技能，以及将技能移入可恢复的回收站。适合需要在 Web 界面维护本地技能的 DSH 用户。使用这些功能不需要额外 API 密钥；按链接安装时会从 GitHub 获取内容。

Skill Center is a DSH Web settings page for managing skills. It lists skills found in DSH roots, shows details and diagnostics, and lets users toggle, create, install, or move skills to a restorable trash. Link installation fetches content from GitHub; no API key is needed.

Skill Center 的技能列表展示从 DSH 技能目录发现的技能、来源、状态和诊断；选择条目可查看说明与正文。它位于 Web 客户端设置面板。
Skill Center 可切换技能启用状态，并把状态写回技能 frontmatter，让 DSH 技能目录同步反映开关；无法解析 frontmatter 的技能不能切换。
Skill Center 支持在选定技能目录新建技能、从链接安装技能，也可把技能移入回收站并在之后恢复。创建和安装均通过 Web 设置面板发起。
Skill Center 使用链接安装技能时会向 GitHub 下载用户提供链接对应的文件或归档；这需要访问 GitHub 主机。

`Modal` stylesheet, so the layout, colours and scrollbar are the ones the application
produces; only the surrounding application window is left out. `scripts/dev/render-shots.mjs`
regenerates them, in either theme.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Where it appears：The composer button lives in `conversation.input.left`. That is the only composer seat a plugin may extend: the permission chip (`conversation.input.permission`) and the model picker (`conversation.input.model`) are `single` seats their own plugins already hold, so nothing can be inserted between them. The button also cannot deep-link to its settings section — `openSection` is internal to the settings shell — so it opens the page directly instead.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · What it does：- **Lists** the skills under `$DSH_HOME/skills` (default `~/.dsh/skills`), any directory the profile adds through `customSkillDirs`, and the current project's `<project>/.dsh/skills`.
- **Shows details** for one skill: description, path, frontmatter block and instruction body.
- **Searches** by name or description, and can hide the switched-off skills.
- **Switches a skill on or off** without losing it: everything else about the file, including your own frontmatter keys, is left alone.
- **Creates a skill** from a name, a description and a body.
- **Installs a skill from a link** — a GitHub repository, a `/tree/` path inside one, a `.zip`, or a single `SKILL.md`.
- **Deletes a skill into a trash**, and restores it from there.
- **Writes new skills where you choose** — the destination control offers every directory the profile makes available, and the host accepts nothing else.
- **Reports problems** the host would silently skip, such as a missing `description` or a name that is not kebab-case.
- Follows the Host's light or dark theme.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Where new skills are written：The destinations come from the Host, not from the panel: `GET /roots` answers with the
profile's configured `customSkillDirs` followed by the default `$DSH_HOME/skills`. The
browser offers exactly that list, and `POST /create` and `POST /install` refuse a
directory outside it — so "choose where to write" does not become "write anywhere". With
one destination the control is a sentence; with several, each is a button, because the
path is the point.
@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Where deletion is allowed to reach：Removing something the user wrote is the one destructive thing here, so it is bounded:
section: Where deletion is allowed to reach

text:
@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Where deletion is allowed to reach：- **Only DSH's own skills.** The trash covers the global roots (the DSH home and any `customSkillDirs`). A project root — `<project>/.dsh/skills`, which is under version control — is never touched: Skill Center may switch such a skill on or off, but it will not move it out of a repository.
- **Only skills DSH can actually load.** A skill with broken frontmatter may have been misread, which is a reason to leave it alone rather than to move it.
- **Never through a link.** A symbolic link, or a Windows junction (which `lstat` reports as an ordinary directory), is refused by comparing the resolved path with the requested one.
- **Never a plain erase.** The bundle is moved into `~/.dsh/skill-center/trash` with a record of where it came from, and the panel can put it back byte-for-byte. Emptying the trash is a separate, confirmed action.
- **Never a half-move.** Everything is validated before anything moves, and a move that cannot be recorded is rolled back. Because `rename` cannot cross volumes, a failed move falls back to copy-then-remove — copy first, so a failure leaves the original in place.
section: Where deletion is allowed to reach

text: @suifengshiqu/skill-center README · What installing a link will and will not do：The download is treated as hostile input: entry paths may not escape the target, a bundle must have a `SKILL.md` with a name DSH accepts and a description DSH requires, an existing name is refused rather than overwritten, and nothing is written until every one of those checks has passed. Private archives and Zip64 are refused. Links to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `.local`) are not fetched, and a single download is capped at 8 MB and 800 entries.
section: What installing a link will and will not do

text: @suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Which layouts are discovered：Matching the Host's own filesystem provider exactly, a skill is a directory bundle `<name>/SKILL.md` or a flat `<name>.md`, **at the top level of a skills root**. Nested `**/SKILL.md` is deliberately not discovered.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Which layouts are discovered：This matters when installing from a GitHub download: a repository ZIP extracts to one folder, and copying *that* folder into `~/.dsh/skills` leaves every bundle one level too deep, where neither DSH nor this panel will find it. Move the bundle folders themselves into the skills root.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · What it does not do：- No other agents' directories (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …).
- No Git repositories, no skill marketplace, no automatic updates.
- No creating or importing skills.
- No Trash.
- Nothing outside the two roots above is ever read or written.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · How switching a skill off works：Skill Center writes the two flags the DSH filesystem provider already understands into the skill's own frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: What it is for.
disable-model-invocation: true

Switching the skill back on removes exactly those two keys, restoring the document byte-for-byte. Because the flags live in the file:

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness with the Web client (tested against `0.2.0-rc.2`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Install：From npm, which needs nothing on the machine but DSH:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add @suifengshiqu/skill-center
```

From source, if you want to change it:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/a766513648-lgtm/dsh-skill-center.git
cd dsh-skill-center
npm install
npm run verify                   # type check, build, tests

Or from a tarball you built yourself:

```powershell
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add .\suifengshiqu-skill-center-0.1.0.tgz
```

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Install：Then **restart DSH** — the host half is loaded once at start-up, so a page refresh
alone is not enough — and open **Settings → Skill Center**.

> Installing this package by its git URL does not work: pnpm refuses to run a
> dependency's build scripts by default, and the published `lib/` is what makes the
> npm route work. Use the registry, or clone and build.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Install：> The client half is served with an immutable cache header and its URL is keyed on
> the bundle's modification time. Reinstalling the same version can therefore leave
> an old page in the browser; a hard reload (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) or a full application
> restart picks the new one up.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Development：```
src/
  index.ts              host half: browser API + the on/off gate provider
  contract.ts           request and response shapes shared by both halves
  core/parse.ts         frontmatter reading and diagnosis

`lib/` is generated; run `npm run build` after changing `src/`.

`.npmrc` is machine-specific and not committed; `.npmrc.example` explains what it
holds and when it is needed.

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Contributing to other plugins' slots：`settings.section` and `conversation.input.left` are declared by other plugins, not by this one. Calling `slots.register` directly races the declarer: whichever plugin activates first throws `slot "settings.section" is not declared (a parent entry's children table must declare it)`. The failure is intermittent — it depends on activation order — and the client plugin loader reports it only as `<name>: failed`, with the reason going to the browser console. Always go through `slots.inject`, which waits for the declaration, re-runs on change and tears the contribution down when the declarer goes away:

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Diagnosing a plugin that will not activate：A plugin that fails to load leaves almost no trace: the desktop reports *"N entries did not activate"* with only `<name>: failed`, and the full reason never reaches the log. These tools answer it:

@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Diagnosing a plugin that will not activate：```powershell
node scripts/probe-host.mjs <path-to-lib/index.js>   # does apply() throw, and what does it call?
node scripts/probe-app.mjs  <path-to-lib/index.js>   # does the plugin mount on a real cordis app?
node scripts/variant.mjs minimal                     # swap in a throwaway page that only reports whether it loaded
```
section: Diagnosing a plugin that will not activate

text: @suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Diagnosing a plugin that will not activate：`probe-host.mjs` catches API misuse; `probe-app.mjs` catches module-shape and mount-semantics problems; the `minimal` variant separates "the client module machinery cannot load this bundle" from "the page itself fails". `variants/` holds both browser halves and `scripts/reinstall.ps1 -Variant minimal` builds, packs and installs one.
section: Diagnosing a plugin that will not activate

text: @suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Why the build does not use a bundler：The development sandbox refuses `spawn` with piped stdio, which is how esbuild's JavaScript API starts its native service. The build therefore uses the TypeScript compiler in process, transpiling each module to CommonJS and emitting:
section: Why the build does not use a bundler

text:
@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Why the build does not use a bundler：- `lib/index.js` — one CommonJS file for the host, with `lib/package.json` marking the folder so the package's own `"type": "module"` does not make Node parse it as ESM;
- `lib/client.js` — one lazy factory in the Web client's module-system format, with an internal module table and Host-shared libraries resolved through the shell's import map.
section: Why the build does not use a bundler

text:
@suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Two rules the artifacts must obey：1. **No runtime `require` of a Host package.** The plugin is installed on its own, so the Host's packages are not on its resolution path. A single side-effect `import '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver'`, added only for its type augmentation, survives bundling and makes the whole plugin fail to import — Settings then shows no page at all. Imports that exist only for types must be `import type`, which TypeScript erases.
2. **Only libraries declared in `dsh.client.external` may be required by the browser half.** Anything else either gets bundled (a second copy of React, which breaks hooks) or resolves to `undefined`.
section: Two rules the artifacts must obey

text: @suifengshiqu/skill-center README · Logging：The host half writes **one line to stderr when it starts**, and otherwise only when something fails (with the stack). That single line is the point: the Loader reports a plugin that fails to activate as `<name>: failed` and nothing else, so without it a broken mount is invisible. The browser half reports its own failures to the host over `/api/skill-center/client-report`, which reaches the same log; it says nothing when it succeeds.
